source/obd/obd_pid.c: table of 19 Mode 01 PIDs (04-09 load, coolant, fuel trims both banks; 0B MAP, 0C RPM, 0D speed, 0E timing, 0F IAT, 10 MAF, 11 throttle, 1F run time, 2F fuel, 33 baro, 42 module V, 46 ambient, 5C oil) with SAE J1979 formulas, decoding to metric from raw bytes or an assembled reply (first ECU with a full answer), and ASCII display text in US (mph, F, inHg) or metric units; trim total and vacuum (baro - MAP) helpers. tests/test_pid.c covers formulas, short / refused / other-PID replies, multi-ECU CAN, formatting and -0 rounding. 139 tests pass with clang and gcc; devkitPro build clean.

source/obd/obd_live.c: one request per step, round-robin over the wanted PIDs the car supports and obd_pid decodes; latest value, time, smoothed refresh rate and read count per PID; ATRV every 5 s (stops asking if refused); a PID dropped after 3 NO DATA / unusable replies in a row; OBD_LIVE_LOST on timeout or I/O error so the caller reconnects; IDLE when nothing is left; manifold vacuum from PID 33 or a MAP read between two RPM-0 reads (an engine start isn't mistaken for baro); overall requests per second. 11 host tests on the fake adapter; emulator check polls every scenario. Running it on the worker thread comes with the LIVE / TRIM screens (3n6.5, 3n6.6).

tools/elm_scenarios.py: ridgeline answers live PIDs 04-09, 0B-0F, 11 at warm idle with both banks' trims (no MAF, no 33), tracker one bank plus MAF, j1850 lean bank 1 trims to match its P0171; values vary between reads. Scenario replies replace the emulator's own entries for the same requests. tools/check-scenarios.sh: all four scenarios pass with live data.

LIVE screen: HOME's LIVE card opens it and starts polling on the worker thread (obd_live; reuses this connection's protocol search, reconnects on loss, stops with a message if the car doesn't answer). Top screen: protocol and requests/s, each PID's value (US units) and refresh rate, adapter battery voltage, vacuum (PID 33 or engine-off MAP). Bottom: toggles for every supported PID (6 a page, green = polled), START / STOP, BACK; choice saved as [live] pids in config.ini (default RPM, speed, coolant, IAT, throttle, load, MAP, timing, MAF). Platform-free text and toggles in source/data/live_view.c with tests. Checked in Azahar against the ridgeline emulator scenario: polling, toggle, STOP, BACK + save. 153 tests pass with clang and gcc; all emulator scenarios pass. The 8 PIDs at 2 Hz target is for the hardware test (3n6.8) after the ISO 9141-2 speed-up (3n6.4).

obd_link_adapter_ready(): only OK / NO_VEHICLE mark a connection's reset as done (diag_scan and LIVE's open), so a failed or lost setup is reset again next time and echo can't stay on. Failed setups now log the command and status (e.g. '! LIVE: Adapter not answering properly (ATE0: Timeout)'). Test added; 157 tests pass with clang and gcc.

obd_pid table has refresh_ms per PID (RPM/speed/throttle/MAP/MAF 0 = as often as possible; STFT, load, timing 500 ms; LTFT, run time, module V 5 s; IAT 10 s; coolant, oil 15 s; fuel 30 s; baro, ambient 60 s). obd_live keeps period and due time per PID and always reads the most overdue (ties in list order); obd_live_set_period for views. LIVE shows slow PIDs as 'every N s'. Tests: priority (coolant waits 15 s while RPM keeps reading), equal periods take turns; existing tests unchanged. 159 tests pass with clang and gcc; all emulator scenarios pass.

Owner log 2026-11-16 10:20 (Ridgeline, ISO 9141-2, build 68ee377), after the socket fix (1b0b2e2) and response count: connect 6 ms (was ~785), ATRV adapter-only 40 ms (was 393), ATDPN 30 ms (was 370), 010C 331 ms (was 631), 010C1 187 ms (was 399). LIVE 5.5 requests/s (was 2.2): Engine view RPM 1.4 Hz, Warm-up RPM 4.5 Hz, All (12 PIDs) fast ones 0.7 Hz. What's left (~187 ms per request) is the ISO 9141-2 bus and the truck's ECU; ATAT2 / ATST19 don't change it. The root cause was the soc single-session contention (conntest's 100 ms poll), not the adapter or Wi-Fi power save. Tracker numbers come with its hardware test (3n6.8).

Owner speed test 2026-11-16 10:20 (Ridgeline): 010C1 187 ms, with ATAT2 187 ms, with ATST19 188 ms. Neither helps once the response count is used (the adapter already returns on the first reply), so LIVE keeps the adapter's defaults (ATAT1, ATST32). The SPEED TEST keeps both sets for other cars (e.g. the CAN Ascent).

TRIM screen: HOME's TRIM card polls 06/08 (fast), 07/09 (1 s), RPM (1 s), speed (2 s) through the LIVE poller. Top: short / long / total per bank as 25-cell center-zero bars (-25..+25 %, 2 % a cell, '<' / '>' past the end) colored green (<=10 %), amber (10-20 %), red (>20 %); one bank when 08/09 aren't supported; engine RPM and idle; hints (both / one bank lean or rich, at idle vs driving, engine off, long-term not learned yet) marked 'Hints, not diagnoses.' Bottom: what trims mean, the color legend, how to check; BACK, START / STOP. Logic platform-free in source/data/trim_view.c (tests/test_trim.c). Checked in Azahar: ridgeline (two banks, normal) and j1850 (one bank, lean +39 %: amber, red, over-range, 'Lean at idle' hint). 165 tests pass with clang and gcc.

diag_has_trim_codes() (P0171 / P0172 / P0174 / P0175 stored or pending; tested). DIAG's bottom row becomes BACK < n/m > TRIM CLEAR SCAN (every button still 5+ cells) when that's true; TRIM opens the TRIM screen and its BACK returns to DIAG. Checked in Azahar with the j1850 scenario (P0171 stored). 166 tests pass with clang and gcc.

obd_pid_parse_multi decodes '41 0C A B 0D C ...' (tests: three PIDs, cut short, unknown PID, wrong service). obd_live with use_multi on CAN (protocols 6-C) sends the most overdue PID plus up to 5 others that are due or have refresh 0, parses every ECU's reply, counts a miss only for PIDs left out; NO DATA or an answer to only the first PID sets multi_refused (one PID a request after, no misses). App turns it on for LIVE and TRIM; LIVE's summary log says which was used. Tests for combined requests, partial replies and both fallbacks; emulator 'car' scenario: 40 of 41 requests combined, all PIDs read; ISO / J1850 scenarios unchanged. 169 tests pass with clang and gcc. Real-car check: the Ascent (gauge-boy-3n6.13).
